draft.title: Combinations
card: A combination is a selection where order does not matter. Choosing Ana and Ben is the same as choosing Ben and Ana.
The number of ways to choose r items from n is nCr = n! ÷ (r! × (n − r)!). Here n! means n × (n − 1) × ... × 1.
A shortcut is 5C2 = (5 × 4) ÷ (2 × 1) = 10. Also nCr = nC(n − r), so 5C2 = 5C3.
draft.remember: If order does not matter, divide the ordered count by r!.

a.why: 6C2 = (6 × 5) ÷ (2 × 1) = 15. The answer 30 is wrong because it is 6 × 5 and does not divide by 2! to remove repeated pairs.

b.q: A coach picks 3 players from a squad of 8 to attend a clinic. The order of picking does not matter. How many different groups can be picked?
b.why: 8C3 = (8 × 7 × 6) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 336 ÷ 6 = 56. The answer 336 counts each group in every order, so it is 6 times too large.

problems.detail: The remember line uses the idea of an 'ordered count', which the card never names or explains. The card only shows the shortcut (5 × 4) ÷ (2 × 1). Students may not see what 'the ordered count' refers to.
The clue spells out the whole calculation ('Divide 8 × 7 × 6 by 3!'), so a student can get 56 by arithmetic alone without knowing how to set up a combination.

proposal.title: Combinations
card: A combination is a selection where order does not matter. Choosing Ana and Ben is the same as choosing Ben and Ana.
The number of ways to choose r items from n is nCr = n! ÷ (r! × (n − r)!). Here n! means n × (n − 1) × ... × 1.
Shortcut: multiply r numbers counting down from n, then divide by r!. So 5C2 = (5 × 4) ÷ (2 × 1) = 10. Dividing by r! removes repeats, as each group can be ordered in r! ways.
proposal.remember: When order does not matter, divide by r! so each group is counted once.

a.why: 6C2 = (6 × 5) ÷ (2 × 1) = 15. The answer 30 is 6 × 5 without dividing by 2!, so it counts each pair twice, once in each order.
a.clue: Each pair can be ordered in 2! ways.

b.q: A coach picks 3 players from a squad of 8 to attend a clinic. The order of picking does not matter. How many different groups can be picked?
b.why: This is 8C3 = (8 × 7 × 6) ÷ (3 × 2 × 1) = 336 ÷ 6 = 56. The answer 336 counts each group in every order, so it is 3! = 6 times too large.
b.clue: Work out which number is n and which is r.
